items.title: Eight equivalent conditions for the vanishing of Ext groups out of a localization at a single element
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring A, an element f, and a complex K in D(A), and establishes the equivalence of six genuine conditions (the seventh entry of the displayed list is the author's placeholder and contributes no mathematics): vanishing of Ext^n_A(A_f, K) for all n, vanishing of Hom in the derived category out of every object of D(A_f), the vanishing of T(K, f), the same condition degreewise on the cohomology, the pair of vanishings of Hom_A(A_f, H^p(K)) and Ext^1_A(A_f, H^p(K)), the vanishing of R Hom_A(A_f, K), and the invertibility of the explicitly displayed pro-product endomorphism (source lines 25849-25866). The proof runs three independent computations: it descends from Ext vanishing to Hom vanishing using a K-injective representative and the adjunction Hom_A(M, I) = Hom_{A_f}(M, Hom_A(A_f, I)) together with the fact that the resulting complex is K-injective and acyclic, hence homotopy equivalent to zero (proof lines 25869-25884); it writes down the explicit two-term free resolution of A_f with the displayed maps and identifies its Hom-dual with the pro-product endomorphism, which yields both the equivalence with condition (7) and the identification of T(K, f) with R Hom_A(A_f, K) (proof lines 25887-25906); and it uses the Ext spectral sequence of a two-term projective resolution, which degenerates at E_2 because the E_2 page then has only two nonzero columns, to obtain the short exact sequences comparing Ext^p_A(A_f, K) with Ext^1 and Hom of the cohomology (proof lines 25909-25932). The non-routine steps are the two-term resolution and the degeneration argument.
